messages:
Jorge (AE): MerchantDelta reached back. They're evaluating a migration from CompetitorZ to Redwood. Main asks: prompt/response parity, how to handle function calls, token accounting differences, and any migration credits. Can SEs start a quick triage?

Maya (SE): On it. Quick checklist: map CompetitorZ 'result.text' -> Redwood 'choices[0].message.content' for chat-mode. CompetitorZ streams line-delimited JSON; Redwood streams SSE. We'll provide a minimal shim example.

Keisha Ops: POC infra Q: they prefer using our Hosted API first, but want an option to move to Dedicated after acceptance. Need IP allowlist and sample network tests.

Dmitri ML: Prompt parity notes: CompetitorZ uses a custom tokenization that counts special markers as single tokens. Expect token-per-prompt variance (often -3% to +5%). Also they set temperature=0.2 by default; we should match that. Recommend running 200-prompt eval and compute top-1 match rate.

Renee (Security): They'll send an infosec questionnaire. Ask: are logs persisted, who can see request payloads, do we support customer-managed KMS? If they require KMS, Private deployment needed (adds ~3-5 weeks).

Maya (SE): Shim snippet to include in POC repo: 
```
# shim: competitorz -> redwood chat mapping
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"${competitor_prompt}"}],"max_tokens":300}'
```
Note: map competitor function-call events to Redwood function handling; function schemas may need normalizing.

Jorge (AE): Pricing question: they asked if we bill per-token or per-request and whether we can offer a time-limited migration credit. billing-bot, can you confirm policy?

billing-bot: hosted product = per-token billing by default; Dedicated = committed monthly capacity pricing. Migration credits considered case-by-case; escalate to Sales Ops.

Dmitri ML: Behavioral diffs: CompetitorZ has a deterministic content filter that rewrites outputs rather than blocking. That caused their NLU ranking tests to differ. Add 'policy-behavior' row to acceptance criteria.

Keisha Ops: Proposed POC acceptance criteria for MerchantDelta: 1) top-1 output match >= 93% over 200 eval prompts, 2) token billing variance < 8% after normalization, 3) latency p95 < 400ms for hosted, 4) SSO + IP allowlist verified.

Renee (Security): Also add data residency check: they need EU-only processing for EU traffic. Hosted EU regions available; confirm with infra.

Maya (SE): I'll assemble: 1) sample shim with streaming example, 2) tokenization diff script, 3) three divergence cases with suggested prompt rewrites, 4) eval harness and scoring script. Push to repo merchantdelta-poc by EOD.

ci-bot: CI started for branch merchantdelta/poc-setup: smoke-tests queued.

Jorge (AE): Perfect. I'll share the POC plan and schedule a sync with MerchantDelta tomorrow 11am CET. I'll include the eval set and acceptance criteria. Thanks team.
